name: error-state
title: Error state
description: The surface that failed, naming the cause and the next action. BDS-042: "something went wrong" leaves the player with nothing to do, which is worse than the error, so `cause`, `label`, `actionLabel` and `onAction` are all required and the control is rendered here rather than passed in, which makes `data-gs-next-action` appear exactly once for a test to count. It does not know what failed: `cause` is host-supplied and so is every word on screen, and `network`, `rejected`, `expired`, `not-found` and `unknown` are the recommended vocabulary rather than a closed set, which is why the prop is a string. It never carries `data-gs-state="wrong"`, because a network failure is not a wrong answer and rendering it as one gives a failed submit a cross and a strikethrough. Two shapes: a centred panel for a surface that failed as a whole, and an inline row for a submit that did not land. Never a modal.
docs: Render it where the failure happened. Pass `cause` as the token your own system already uses for the failure, `label` as the short line a player reads, the children for what was lost and what was not, and `actionLabel` with `onAction` for the next step. Pass `causeWord` so the accessible name says the cause in words rather than in a token. Pass `layout="inline"` for a submit that did not land, and leave it at `panel` for a surface that failed as a whole. Reach for `empty-state` instead when there is simply nothing to show: an absence is not a failure, and reporting one as the other invents a cause.
